call_points.text: Management guided for an 80% revenue growth for the current fiscal year with an EBITDA margin of 24% ±100 bps.
Phase 3 expansion for fuel cells to be completed at the new facility by March 2027.
Closing order book ₹5,143 Cr at end-Q1FY27, plus ₹800 Cr of orders received on the call day.
Fuel cell expansion in three phases: Phase 1 commissioned, Phase 2 by September-October, Phase 3 by March 2027.
Nuclear: ₹684 Cr of orders today, about ₹130 Cr more expected this quarter, execution starting H2FY27 over about three years.
Data centre infrastructure: about ₹45 Cr order to execute by February-March, with a potential requirement of eight such sets a year.
Aerospace and defence revenue expected to double this fiscal year, with a 3-4 year ramp from that base.
Longer-term ambition: products business above ₹1,000 Cr and aerospace ₹600-700 Cr, without a stated date.
Asked about interest cost split, the MD said he did not have the break-up and deferred to the CFO.
On US data centre capex delay concerns, management dismissed them as "unwanted noise" without giving numbers.
Phase 3 fuel cell capacity size was not disclosed, citing an NDA with the customer.
FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 80% plus/minus 5% with EBITDA margin around 24%.

operating_notes.text: Received highest order inflows of ₹2,453.3 Cr in FY26.
Received international blanket purchase orders worth USD 238.76 million (₹2,278.96 Crores) from an existing customer.
Working capital days improved to 172 days in FY26 from 278 days in Q2FY26.
Received purchase orders worth ₹467.30 Cr (USD 48.68 mn) from an international customer, execution 50% by March 2027 and 50% by June 2027.
Promoter Kavitha Reddy Gangapatnam released pledge on 1,77,000 shares upon loan repayment, leaving 43,000 shares (0.14%) encumbered.
Nuclear order book of ₹684 Cr today, with about ₹130 Cr more expected this quarter, to be executed within roughly three years; MTAR says it holds a 60-70% share of orders for these reactors.
Data centre infrastructure order of about ₹45 Cr to be executed by February-March, against a potential requirement of eight such sets a year, all for export.
Domestic defence opportunity in actuator assemblies for LCA Tejas Mark-1A is about ₹140-150 Cr, with overall domestic defence opportunity potential above ₹250 Cr.
Secured orders worth ₹1,207.2 Cr across various sectors during Q2FY27, taking the order book to ₹5,976.5 Cr as of 30 September 2026.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹306.07 Cr (+67.2% YoY), net profit ₹44.28 Cr (+222.7% YoY).
MTAR Technologies released its investor presentation for May 2026, highlighting FY26 revenue of ₹876.2 Cr and an order book of ₹2,581.9 Cr.
PRIYANKA AGARWAL, Company Secretary, uploaded Q4 FY 2025-26 earnings call recording on 13 May 2026 at 11:00 AM (IST) via https://mtar.in.
Mtar Technologies received international blanket purchase orders worth ₹2,278.96 Crores from an undisclosed customer.
2026-05-20: MTAR Technologies reported Q4 and FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹876.21 Cr and raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 80%.
MTAR Technologies received international purchase orders worth ₹467.30 Cr (USD 48.68 mn) for execution by June 2027.
Promoter Kavitha Reddy Gangapatnam released pledge on 1,77,000 shares (0.58% stake) following loan repayment.

On 30 July 2026 MTAR's Q1FY27 call reported revenue of ₹360.7 Cr (up 130.4% YoY), EBITDA of ₹85.1 Cr and PAT of ₹50.2 Cr, with a closing order book of ₹5,143 Cr plus ₹800 Cr of orders received that day.
H1FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹767.49 Cr, net profit ₹110.06 Cr.
NCLT sanctioned the merger of wholly owned subsidiaries Gee Pee Aerospace and Magnatar Aero Systems into MTAR Technologies.
MTAR Technologies released its October 2026 Investor Presentation detailing Q2FY27 financial performance and strategic expansion plans.
MTAR Technologies submitted a revised Q2FY27 investor presentation on 30 October 2026 to rectify reporting errors.
Audio recording of Q2 FY 2026-27 earnings conference call held 30 Oct 2026 uploaded on company website.
